<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Check KV loaded back from KV offloading against checksums stored with it, and implement it for `MooncakeStoreConnector`. Each stored checksum is bound to the block it was stored for, so a value that is intact but belongs to another prefix fails the check like corrupted KV.

Stacked on #62211 (connector-agnostic KV checksums for P/D): the first commit adds the offloading contract to it, the second implements it for the Mooncake store. Review only the last two commits until #62211 merges.

## Claims

- With `enable_kv_checksum`, `MooncakeStoreConnector` stores each block's checksum with the block's KV, and every load from the store is checked against it, per block, with the same kernel and scheduler path as P/D loads.
- The stored checksum is XORed with a tag of the block's hash and its KV cache group's layers. The scheduler removes the tag that the request's own block hashes give for each position before it compares. KV at the wrong position or from another TP/PP shard already fails, as #62211 weighs every piece by its token position, head and layer; the tag adds a value stored for the same position of another prefix (another request's key, a reused or late-written value, e.g. kvcache-ai/Mooncake#4491) and a value stored by a model with other layers or dtypes.
- A failed check is a KV load failure (`kv_load_failure_policy`), and the failing blocks are removed from the store on every rank, so later requests do not load them again.
- Layouts that cannot carry the checksums (store TP sharding, non-full-attention groups, hash block size != block size, `custom_mem_pool`, HiSparse) are reported at startup instead of left silently unchecked.
- No change to P/D loads or to deployments with checksums disabled.

Out of scope: KV that never leaves the GPU (e.g. a kernel reading past a request's own blocks). These checksums only check KV that is loaded from elsewhere.

## Validation

Unit tests:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_checksum.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_checksum_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_*.py
```

- GB200: 557 passed.
- macOS (CPU, Triton-kernel tests skip): 421 passed, 153 skipped (`test_multi_example_connector_consistency` deselected: it needs the gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`).
- `test_offloaded_kv_load_is_checked_against_its_checksums[True-other_prefix]` loads intact KV whose checksums were stored for the same positions of another request. Without the tag (the save call reverted to the old signature) the load passes the check, so this case fails (`assert set() == {'id-1'}`; the other 5 cases pass); with the tag both positions fail and all 6 pass (GB200).

End to end on GB200, Qwen3-8B, `MooncakeStoreConnector` (`kv_both`) with `enable_kv_checksum`, TP1. Instance A stores 16 4k-token prompts; instance B, with an empty GPU cache and the same `mooncake_master`, serves them from the store; C (no connector) is a reference.

| Injected into one stored key before B reads | without the tag (d04eb27b0a) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| nothing | — | 0 mismatches, external prefix cache hits 61696 / 61718 |
| the intact value of the same block position of the previous prompt | not detected: loaded, 0 mismatches, key kept | detected: 1 block removed, key gone |
| 256 bytes flipped | detected (earlier run) | detected: 1 block removed, key gone |

On detection B logs `Removing 1 Mooncake store blocks of request ... that failed their KV checksums.`, the key is gone right after, and the request is recomputed. In the uninjected run and the misplacement run, A and B ran with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`: no sync violations.

Earlier runs of the same setup before the tag was added (same storage layout, the stored value differs only by the XOR):

- TP1 and TP2: B's external prefix cache hit rate 99.6% (every full block; the partial last block is recomputed), 0 mismatches, 0 load failures. Outputs vs. A and vs. C differ in the usual cross-instance way (TP2: B==A 5/8, B==C 6/8, A==C 6/8).
- Overhead on store hits, checksums on vs. off, median of 3 rounds:

  | prompt, concurrency | TTFT p50 on | TTFT p50 off | tok/s on | tok/s off |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 4k, 1 | 359.0 ms | 368.4 ms | 22.2 | 21.6 |
  | 4k, 16 | 2116.7 ms | 2147.0 ms | 43.9 | 41.9 |
  | 16k, 1 | 1242.9 ms | 1271.9 ms | 10.0 | 9.7 |
  | 16k, 16 | 6942.3 ms | 7276.1 ms | 12.6 | 12.3 |

  No measurable overhead. These loads go over TCP and dominate TTFT, so this does not bound the overhead relative to a faster (RDMA) load; the checksum kernels themselves are measured in #62211. The tag adds one 8-byte-per-block host-to-device copy per save and a NumPy XOR per checked block on the scheduler.

Setup: `mooncake-transfer-engine` 0.3.13.post1, `protocol: tcp`, both instances with `MC_TCP_MAX_QUEUED_TRANSFERS_PER_PEER=65535 MC_TCP_MAX_PENDING_ADMISSIONS_PER_PEER=65535 MC_TCP_ADMISSION_TIMEOUT_MS=60000`. Without them every cross-instance store read fails (-800 after a 60 s timeout), with or without KV checksums: one 4k-token load is 240 keys x 36 regions, far over the default per-peer queue of 1024 transfers.

CI: the new tests are in existing files that CI already runs; the Triton-kernel ones need a GPU.

## Details

**Contract** (first commit). The checksum worker gives a connector a `(num_blocks,)` int64 device tensor (`init_block_checksums`) and fills the entries of full blocks before the connector offloads them (`save_block_checksums`). The connector passes each block's hash with it, moves a block's entry wherever it moves the block's KV, and writes it back before it reports the load finished. `get_kv_checksum_sources(request)` names the cache tiers whose loads bring the checksums back; such an asynchronous load is checksummed on its finishing step and compared per block by the scheduler. `on_kv_checksum_failure` lets the connector drop the bad KV.

**Why the tag.** A P/D load is checked against a reference that comes from the producer of the same request, separately from the KV, so KV from the wrong place cannot match it. An offloaded checksum travels with its KV, so on its own it only shows that a value is internally consistent. The checksum already depends on the token position, head and layer, so KV loaded at the wrong position or into another shard fails; what it cannot tell is whether the value at the right position belongs to this prefix. The tag (`block_checksum_tags`: `block_hash[:8] ^ group fingerprint`) binds the stored checksum to what the reader expects: the block hash covers the prefix tokens, LoRA, multimodal inputs and cache salt, and the fingerprint (from #62211) covers the group's layer names, types and dtypes. The scheduler derives the expected tag from `request.block_hashes`, not from the store. Leaving the rank out of the tag keeps replicas' stored checksums equal. P/D is unchanged. The tag adds no new requirement: cross-instance hits already need reproducible block hashes, since they are the store keys.

**Mooncake store** (second commit). The checksum tensor is registered with the store and appended as one more 8-byte region of every value, so put and get carry a block's entry with its KV and need no extra round trip. `wait_for_save` queues the checksums, with the blocks' hashes from the request, before the CUDA event the sending thread waits on. Keys are rank-local because each rank checks its own shard; values with checksums use a separate key namespace (`@kv_checksums`), so they never mix with values stored without one, at the cost of not reusing blocks stored before checksums were enabled. On failure, rank 0 runs `batch_remove(keys, force=True)` over the LookupKey channel (new `REMOVE_MSG`); force is needed because the failing load still holds a read lease.

**Size.** About 330 non-test lines in the first commit and 260 in the second, most of it the per-block plumbing in the checksum worker and scheduler and the Mooncake register/put/get/remove paths; the tag itself is about 30.

**Limitations.** Synchronous loads (`load_async=False`) are not checked; Mooncake store asserts asynchronous loads. This detects misplaced values; it does not fix their cause (kvcache-ai/Mooncake#4491 should be fixed in Mooncake).

**Not a duplicate.** #57912 adds CRC32C for the filesystem offload tier; this reuses #62211's GPU checksums and its scheduler path, and covers the Mooncake store.

One scenario from Mooncake Issue(https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/issues/4491), I'm unsure this can catch: a batch_get times out, stored_requests[req_id] hits zero, and vLLM releases the KV block—but the underlying RDMA writes may still be in flight. If Request B then reuses that block, we have two concurrent writers to the same memory. Since the checksum is a post-hoc snapshot (computed after the producer considers the write "done"), it seems like a late-arriving write after that snapshot—or a checksum computed during the race—wouldn't be detected at the moment of concurrent write, only (maybe) by a future consumer.

So does this PR actually defend against this concurrent-write-to-the-same-block case, or is that outside what a post-hoc checksum can detect? +# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""KV checksum cost of the Triton kernel.
+
+Checksums ``--num-blocks`` blocks of ``--num-layers`` layers of one layout, in
+one launch, as a consumer does for a finished load and a producer for a
+finished prefill.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_checksum import worker as checksum_worker
+from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_checksum.checksum import MAX_KV_HEADS_PER_LAYER
+from vllm.triton_utils import triton
+
+
+def main(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
+    # Per layer: [blocks, heads, tokens, K and V of head_size] bf16, as 8-byte
+    # pieces.
+    caches = [
+        torch.randn(
+            args.cache_blocks,
+            args.heads,
+            args.block_size,
+            2 * args.head_size,
+            dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            device="cuda",
+        )
+        for _ in range(args.num_layers)
+    ]
+    pieces = [
+        cache.view(torch.int64).unflatten(0, (args.cache_blocks, 1)) for cache in caches
+    ]
+    block_ids = torch.randperm(args.cache_blocks, device="cuda")[: args.num_blocks]
+    first_tokens = torch.arange(args.num_blocks, device="cuda") * args.block_size
+    valid_tokens = torch.full_like(block_ids, args.block_size)
+    layer_bytes = caches[0][0].numel() * caches[0].element_size()
+    gigabytes = block_ids.numel() * layer_bytes * args.num_layers / 1e9
+
+    views = [
+        checksum_worker._LayerView(
+            layer_pieces,
+            first_slice=layer * MAX_KV_HEADS_PER_LAYER,
+            replica_key=(1, 0),
+        )
+        for layer, layer_pieces in enumerate(pieces)
+    ]
+    launch = checksum_worker._FusedLayers(views, columns=[0] * len(views))
+    out = torch.zeros_like(block_ids).unsqueeze(1)
+    ms = triton.testing.do_bench(
+        lambda: launch.accumulate(block_ids, first_tokens, valid_tokens, out)
+    )
+    print(f"{ms:8.3f} ms  {gigabytes / ms * 1e3:8.1f} GB/s of KV read")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--num-layers", type=int, default=1)
+    parser.add_argument("--num-blocks", type=int, default=2048)
+    parser.add_argument("--cache-blocks", type=int, default=8192)
+    parser.add_argument("--heads", type=int, default=8)
+    parser.add_argument("--block-size", type=int, default=16)
+    parser.add_argument("--head-size", type=int, default=128)
+    main(parser.parse_args())

+def _logical_kv(
+    heads: int, seed: int = 0, tokens: int = BLOCK_SIZE, cell_bytes: int = CELL_BYTES
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Random logical KV bytes of one layer: [blocks, heads, tokens, cell]."""
+    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    return torch.randint(
+        0,
+        256,
+        (NUM_BLOCKS, heads, tokens, cell_bytes),
+        generator=gen,

+    )

+def _cache(logical: torch.Tensor, *, token_major=False, kernel_split=1):
+    """A bf16 [B, H, N, C] cache view holding ``logical``, in a given layout."""
+    blocks, heads, tokens, cell = logical.shape
+    data = logical.view(blocks, heads, kernel_split, tokens // kernel_split, cell)
+    data = data.permute(0, 2, 1, 3, 4).reshape(
+        blocks * kernel_split, heads, tokens // kernel_split, cell
+    )
+    if token_major:
+        storage = torch.empty(
+            blocks * kernel_split,
+            tokens // kernel_split,
+            heads,
+            cell,
+            dtype=torch.uint8,
+            device=DEVICE,
+        )
+        view = storage.permute(0, 2, 1, 3)
+    else:
+        view = torch.empty_like(data, device=DEVICE)
+    view.copy_(data)
+    return view.view(torch.bfloat16)

+def _reference(
+    layers: dict[int, torch.Tensor], blocks: KVChecksumBlocks = BLOCKS
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Checksums from the definition: each (layer, head) slice of a block is
+    s = sum_j x_j * (2j + 1) over its 8-byte pieces, numbered in token order
+    from the request's first token, and the block's checksum is sum m * s with
+    m = 2 * (layer * H + head) + 1.
+
+    ``layers`` maps layer numbers to the KV of all their heads.
+    """
+    start, block_ids = blocks.groups[0]
+    sums = np.zeros(len(block_ids), dtype=np.uint64)
+    for number, kv in layers.items():
+        pieces = kv.contiguous().view(torch.int64).numpy().view(np.uint64)
+        _, heads, tokens, num_pieces = pieces.shape
+        head = np.arange(heads, dtype=np.uint64)[:, None, None]
+        token = np.arange(tokens, dtype=np.uint64)[None, :, None]
+        piece = np.arange(num_pieces, dtype=np.uint64)[None, None, :]
+        slice_factor = np.uint64(2) * (
+            np.uint64(number * MAX_KV_HEADS_PER_LAYER) + head
+        ) + np.uint64(1)
+        for row, block_id in enumerate(block_ids):
+            first_token = np.uint64((start + row) * tokens)
+            position = (first_token + token) * np.uint64(num_pieces) + piece
+            weights = slice_factor * (np.uint64(2) * position + np.uint64(1))
+            block = pieces[block_id].copy()
+            block[:, max(0, blocks.num_tokens - (start + row) * tokens) :, :] = 0
+            with np.errstate(over="ignore"):
+                sums[row] += (block * weights).sum(dtype=np.uint64)
+    return sums
+

+def _results(
+    *finished_recving: str, failed: Iterable[str] = ()
+) -> KVConnectorTransferResults:
+    """A connector's transfer results with these loads finished."""
+    return KVConnectorTransferResults(
+        finished_recving=set(finished_recving), failed_recving=set(failed)
+    )

+def _finish(pending: PendingKVChecksums | None) -> KVChecksumRecord:
+    """Copy the checksums to host as the model runner does, and wait."""
+    assert pending is not None
+    record = pending.enqueue_async_cpu_copy()
+    if torch.accelerator.is_available():
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    return record

+def _send_record(worker: KVChecksumWorker, blocks=BLOCKS) -> KVChecksumRecord:
+    worker.bind(KVChecksumScheduled(reqs_to_send={"req": blocks}))
+    return _finish(worker.post_forward(_results(), set()))

+def _send(worker: KVChecksumWorker, blocks=BLOCKS):

+    worker.bind(KVChecksumScheduled(reqs_to_recv={"req": blocks}))
+    record = _finish(worker.post_forward(_results("req"), set()))

+# conv (4 x 8 bf16 = 64 bytes) and ssm (2 x 8 fp32 = 64 bytes): 16 pieces,
+# then an extra state (5 fp32 = 20 bytes) that is not checksummed.
+MAMBA_SHAPES = ((4, 8), (2, 8), (5,))
+MAMBA_DTYPES = (torch.bfloat16, torch.float32, torch.float32)
+MAMBA_COVERED_BYTES = 128

+
+def _mamba_spec(shapes=MAMBA_SHAPES, dtypes=MAMBA_DTYPES, **kwargs) -> MambaSpec:
+    return MambaSpec(block_size=10000, shapes=shapes, dtypes=dtypes, **kwargs)

+def _mamba_cache(
+    content_bytes: int, page_bytes: int, seed: int = 0
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """A Mamba layer's ``[blocks, 1, 1, content]`` int8 cache view over padded
+    pages, as bound by the model runner, and the pages it views."""
+    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    pages = torch.randint(
+        0, 256, (NUM_BLOCKS, page_bytes), generator=gen, dtype=torch.uint8
+    ).to(DEVICE)
+    view = pages[:, :content_bytes].view(torch.int8).view(NUM_BLOCKS, 1, 1, -1)
+    return view, pages
+
+
+def _mamba_reference(
+    states: dict[int, torch.Tensor],
+    block_id: int,
+    covered_bytes: int = MAMBA_COVERED_BYTES,
+) -> np.uint64:
+    """The definition for Mamba state: per (layer, state shard) the slice of
+    the covered state bytes, s = sum_j x_j * (2j + 1), weighted by
+    m = 2 * (layer * H + shard) + 1. ``states`` maps layer * H + shard to its
+    pages."""
+    total = np.uint64(0)
+    for slice_index, pages in states.items():
+        pieces = pages[block_id, :covered_bytes].cpu()
+        x = pieces.view(torch.int64).numpy().view(np.uint64)
+        j = np.arange(len(x), dtype=np.uint64)
+        with np.errstate(over="ignore"):
+            s = (x * (np.uint64(2) * j + np.uint64(1))).sum(dtype=np.uint64)
+            total += (np.uint64(2) * np.uint64(slice_index) + np.uint64(1)) * s
+    return total
+

+MAMBA_BLOCKS = KVChecksumBlocks(num_tokens=39, groups={0: (0, [3])})

+    )

+def _misaligned_cache() -> torch.Tensor:
+    """A cache view starting 2 bytes into its storage."""
+    flat = _bf16_cache(NUM_BLOCKS).flatten()
+    return torch.cat([flat[:1], flat])[1:].view_as(_bf16_cache(NUM_BLOCKS))

+# A TP-split Mamba2 layer, globally: conv [x, B, C] of 8 rows each by 3 bf16
+# columns, and a temporal state of 8 heads of 2 x 2 fp32.
+SPLIT_ROWS = 8
+
+
+def _split_states(fp32_conv: bool = False) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
+    conv = torch.randint(-(2**31), 2**31, (3 * SPLIT_ROWS, 3), generator=gen)
+    temporal = torch.randint(-(2**31), 2**31, (SPLIT_ROWS, 2, 2), generator=gen)
+    temporal = temporal.to(torch.int32).view(torch.float32)
+    if fp32_conv:
+        return conv.to(torch.int32).view(torch.float32), temporal
+    return conv.to(torch.int16).view(torch.bfloat16), temporal
+
+
+def _split_layer(
+    states: tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor],
+    tp_size: int,
+    rank: int,
+    one_group: bool = False,
+    dim_first: bool = True,
+) -> tuple[MambaSpec, torch.Tensor]:
+    """A rank's spec and ``[blocks, 1, 1, state]`` cache with its shard of
+    the global ``states`` in block 3. With ``one_group``, every rank holds B
+    and C whole, as with a single Mamba2 group."""
+    conv, temporal = states
+    rows = SPLIT_ROWS // tp_size
+    shard = slice(rank * rows, (rank + 1) * rows)
+    x, b, c = conv.split(SPLIT_ROWS)
+    if one_group:
+        group_rows, replicas = SPLIT_ROWS, tp_size
+        local_conv = torch.cat([x[shard], b, c])
+    else:
+        group_rows, replicas = rows, 1
+        local_conv = torch.cat([x[shard], b[shard], c[shard]])
+    if not dim_first:
+        local_conv = local_conv.T.contiguous()
+    local_temporal = temporal[shard].contiguous()
+    spec = _mamba_spec(
+        shapes=(tuple(local_conv.shape), tuple(local_temporal.shape)),
+        dtypes=(local_conv.dtype, local_temporal.dtype),
+        state_splits=(
+            MambaStateSplit(
+                0 if dim_first else 1,
+                ((rows, 1), (group_rows, replicas), (group_rows, replicas)),
+            ),
+            MambaStateSplit(0, ((rows, 1),)),
+        ),
+    )
+    content = torch.cat(
+        [t.view(torch.uint8).flatten() for t in (local_conv, local_temporal)]
+    )
+    cache, pages = _mamba_cache(len(content), len(content) + 8, seed=rank)
+    pages[3, : len(content)] = content
+    return spec, cache
+
+
+def _split_reference(states: tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]) -> np.uint64:
+    """The definition for TP-split Mamba state: one slice per global row (the
+    conv rows, then the temporal heads), whose pieces are its elements read
+    unsigned."""
+    conv, temporal = states
+    total = np.uint64(0)
+    for row, data in enumerate([*conv, *temporal]):
+        unsigned = np.uint16 if data.element_size() == 2 else np.uint32
+        x = data.contiguous().view(
+            torch.int16 if unsigned == np.uint16 else torch.int32
+        )
+        x = x.flatten().numpy().view(unsigned).astype(np.uint64)
+        j = np.arange(len(x), dtype=np.uint64)
+        m = np.uint64(2 * (2 * MAX_KV_HEADS_PER_LAYER + row) + 1)
+        with np.errstate(over="ignore"):
+            total += m * (x * (np.uint64(2) * j + np.uint64(1))).sum(dtype=np.uint64)
+    return total
+
+
+def _split_workers(
+    states, tp_size, **kwargs
+) -> tuple[list[KVChecksumWorker], list[torch.Tensor]]:
+    workers, caches = [], []
+    for rank in range(tp_size):
+        spec, cache = _split_layer(states, tp_size, rank, **kwargs)
+        caches.append(cache)
+        workers.append(
+            _worker(
+                _config(_group(spec, _mamba_name(2))),
+                {_mamba_name(2): cache},
+                tp_rank=rank,
+                tp_size=tp_size,
+            )
+        )
+    return workers, caches
+

+with real checksum workers, for NIXL pull (checksums in kv_transfer_params),
+NIXL push and Mooncake (checksums in the connector's messages): the consumer

+from .utils import (

+    create_vllm_config,
+)
+
+# KV checksums are computed by a Triton kernel, on CUDA, ROCm or XPU.
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not kv_checksum_platform_supported(), reason="needs a GPU with Triton"
+)
+
+DEVICE = current_platform.device_type
+
+BLOCK_SIZE = 16
+NUM_BLOCKS = 32
+NUM_TOKENS = 40  # Three blocks, the last one partial.
+HEADS = 2
+CELL_BYTES = 32  # K + V of 8 bf16 values.
+# The checksummed group's layers, split across PP stages.
+LAYERS = ["model.layers.0.self_attn.attn", "model.layers.1.self_attn.attn"]
+# A second group, standing in for one a worker cannot checksum.
+EXTRA_LAYER = "model.layers.2.self_attn.attn"
+# A Mamba (GDN) layer: conv 4 x 8 bf16 and ssm 2 x 8 fp32 per TP rank, 128
+# bytes in a 160-byte page. With prefix caching its states align to the
+# attention blocks: a request's row ends with its running state, then one
+# speculative scratch block.
+MAMBA_LAYER = "model.layers.3.linear_attn"
+MAMBA_SPEC = MambaSpec(
+    block_size=BLOCK_SIZE,
+    shapes=((4, 8), (2, 8)),
+    dtypes=(torch.bfloat16, torch.float32),
+    mamba_type=MambaAttentionBackendEnum.GDN_ATTN,
+    mamba_cache_mode="align",
+    num_speculative_blocks=1,
+)
+MAMBA_STATE_BYTES, MAMBA_PAGE_BYTES = 128, 160
+
+
+def _split_mamba_spec(tp_size: int) -> MambaSpec:
+    """A Mamba2 layer with one group, whose TP split is known: conv [x, B, C]
+    of 4, 2 and 2 rows by 8 bf16 columns, B and C held whole by every rank,
+    and a temporal state of 2 heads of 8 fp32, globally."""
+    x, heads = 4 // tp_size, 2 // tp_size
+    return MambaSpec(
+        block_size=BLOCK_SIZE,
+        shapes=((x + 4, 8), (heads, 8)),
+        dtypes=(torch.bfloat16, torch.float32),
+        mamba_type=MambaAttentionBackendEnum.MAMBA2,
+        mamba_cache_mode="align",
+        num_speculative_blocks=1,
+        state_splits=(
+            MambaStateSplit(0, ((x, 1), (2, tp_size), (2, tp_size))),
+            MambaStateSplit(0, ((heads, 1),)),
+        ),
+    )
+
+
+def _split_shard(conv: torch.Tensor, temporal: torch.Tensor, tp_size, rank):
+    """A rank's state bytes of the global ``_split_mamba_spec`` states."""
+    x, heads = 4 // tp_size, 2 // tp_size
+    local_conv = torch.cat([conv[rank * x : (rank + 1) * x], conv[4:]])
+    local_temporal = temporal[rank * heads : (rank + 1) * heads]
+    return torch.cat(
+        [
+            t.contiguous().view(torch.uint8).flatten()
+            for t in (local_conv, local_temporal)
+        ]
+    )
+
+
+def _kv_cache_config(
+    heads: int,
+    layers: list[str],
+    extra_group: bool = False,
+    mamba_spec: MambaSpec | None = None,
+    block_size: int = BLOCK_SIZE,
+) -> KVCacheConfig:
+    spec = FullAttentionSpec(
+        block_size=block_size, num_kv_heads=heads, head_size=8, dtype=torch.bfloat16
+    )
+    groups = [KVCacheGroupSpec(layers, spec)]
+    if extra_group:
+        groups.append(KVCacheGroupSpec([EXTRA_LAYER], spec))
+    if mamba_spec is not None:
+        groups.append(KVCacheGroupSpec([MAMBA_LAYER], mamba_spec))
+    return KVCacheConfig(
+        num_blocks=NUM_BLOCKS, kv_cache_tensors=[], kv_cache_groups=groups
+    )
+
+
+class _Engine:
+    """A scheduler and its workers' checksum workers over one logical KV cache
+    per layer, standing in for the model runner and the connector's
+    transfers."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        kv_role: str,
+        connector: str = "NixlConnector",
+        tp_size: int = 1,
+        pp_size: int = 1,
+        policy: str = "fail",
+        extra_group: str | None = None,
+        mamba: bool | str = False,
+        block_size: int = BLOCK_SIZE,
+    ):
+        """``extra_group``: None, or whether the workers can checksum a second
+        group ("covered"), skip it for lack of a cache ("skipped"), or leave
+        it out as it holds a drafter layer ("draft").
+        ``mamba``: add a Mamba group, as hybrid models have; "split" for one
+        whose TP split is known (``_split_mamba_spec``)."""
+        vllm_config = create_vllm_config(
+            kv_connector=connector,
+            kv_role=kv_role,
+            block_size=block_size,
+            kv_load_failure_policy=policy,
+        )
+        kv_transfer_config = vllm_config.kv_transfer_config
+        kv_transfer_config.enable_kv_checksum = True
+        vllm_config.parallel_config.tensor_parallel_size = tp_size
+        vllm_config.parallel_config.pipeline_parallel_size = pp_size
+        if mamba:
+            vllm_config.scheduler_config.disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager = False
+            vllm_config.cache_config.mamba_cache_mode = "align"
+        stages = [LAYERS[i::pp_size] for i in range(pp_size)]
+        has_extra = extra_group is not None
+        self.split_mamba = mamba == "split"
+        mamba_spec = (
+            (_split_mamba_spec(tp_size) if self.split_mamba else MAMBA_SPEC)
+            if mamba
+            else None
+        )
+        self.tp_size = tp_size
+        # Like the engine's, the scheduler's config is the first worker's.
+        self.connector = connector
+        scheduler_config = _kv_cache_config(
+            HEADS, stages[0], has_extra, mamba_spec, block_size
+        )
+        self.scheduler = create_scheduler(vllm_config, kv_cache_config=scheduler_config)
+        self.mamba_group = len(scheduler_config.kv_cache_groups) - 1 if mamba else None
+        self.block_size = block_size
+        # Per layer, [blocks, heads, tokens, cell] bytes; ranks view their heads.
+        self.kv = {
+            layer: torch.zeros(
+                NUM_BLOCKS,
+                HEADS,
+                block_size,
+                CELL_BYTES,
+                dtype=torch.uint8,
+                device=DEVICE,
+            )
+            for layer in LAYERS
+        }
+        # Per TP rank, the Mamba layer's state pages (its own shard).
+        self.states = [
+            torch.zeros(
+                NUM_BLOCKS, 2 * MAMBA_PAGE_BYTES, dtype=torch.uint8, device=DEVICE
+            )
+            for _ in range(tp_size)
+        ]
+        replicas = max(1, tp_size // HEADS)
+        heads_per_rank = max(1, HEADS // tp_size)
+        self.workers = []
+        for pp_rank, layers in enumerate(stages):
+            for tp_rank in range(tp_size):
+                first = tp_rank // replicas * heads_per_rank
+                caches = {
+                    layer: self.kv[layer][:, first : first + heads_per_rank].view(
+                        torch.bfloat16
+                    )
+                    for layer in layers
+                }
+                if extra_group in ("covered", "draft"):
+                    caches[EXTRA_LAYER] = torch.zeros_like(caches[layers[0]])
+                if mamba_spec is not None:
+                    # The model runner's [blocks, 1, 1, state] int8 page view.
+                    content = mamba_spec.state_content_size_bytes
+                    state = self.states[tp_rank][:, :content]
+                    caches[MAMBA_LAYER] = state.view(torch.int8)[:, None, None, :]
+                self.workers.append(
+                    KVChecksumWorker(
+                        _kv_cache_config(
+                            heads_per_rank, layers, has_extra, mamba_spec, block_size
+                        ),
+                        caches,
+                        tp_rank=tp_rank,
+                        tp_size=tp_size,
+                        pp_rank=pp_rank,
+                        uniform_kv_heads=HEADS,
+                        draft_layer_names=frozenset(
+                            [EXTRA_LAYER] if extra_group == "draft" else []
+                        ),
+                    )
+                )
+
+    def schedule(self) -> SchedulerOutput:
+        output = self.scheduler.schedule()
+        for worker in self.workers:
+            worker.bind(output.kv_checksum_scheduled)
+        return output
+
+    def finish_step(
+        self,
+        output: SchedulerOutput,
+        finished_recving: set[str] | None = None,
+        received: dict[str, bytes] | None = None,
+    ):
+        """Run the workers' post_forward and the scheduler's update.
+
+        ``received``: checksums the connector received with the loads.
+        """
+        checksums = []
+        for worker in self.workers:
+            pending = worker.post_forward(
+                KVConnectorTransferResults(
+                    finished_recving=finished_recving or set(),
+                    kv_checksums=received or {},
+                ),
+                output.finished_req_ids,
+            )
+            if pending is not None:
+                checksums.append(pending.enqueue_async_cpu_copy())
+        requests = [self.scheduler.requests[i] for i in output.num_scheduled_tokens]
+        model_runner_output = create_model_runner_output(requests)
+        # Like the model runner, sample nothing for a prefill not yet done.
+        for i, request in enumerate(requests):
+            if request.is_prefill_chunk:
+                model_runner_output.sampled_token_ids[i] = []
+        model_runner_output.kv_connector_output = KVConnectorOutput(
+            finished_recving=finished_recving, kv_checksums=checksums or None
+        )

+def _block_ids(output: SchedulerOutput, req_id: str, send: bool) -> tuple[int, list]:
+    scheduled = output.kv_checksum_scheduled

+@dataclass

+def _state_block(
+    engine: _Engine, output: SchedulerOutput, req_id: str, send: bool

+    row's last block before the speculative scratch blocks. Also checks that

+    scheduled = output.kv_checksum_scheduled
+    assert scheduled is not None
+    blocks = (scheduled.reqs_to_send if send else scheduled.reqs_to_recv)[req_id]

+def _prefill(producer: _Engine, request: Request) -> _Transfer:
+    """Prefill ``request`` on the producer, leaving the KV in its blocks."""
+    if producer.connector == "MooncakeConnector":
+        assert request.kv_transfer_params is not None
+        request.kv_transfer_params["transfer_id"] = f"xfer-{request.request_id}"
+    producer.scheduler.add_request(request)
+    # Prefill may take several steps (Mamba states align chunks to blocks).
+    output = producer.schedule()
+    for _ in range(NUM_TOKENS):
+        scheduled = output.kv_checksum_scheduled
+        if scheduled is not None and request.request_id in scheduled.reqs_to_send:
+            break
+        producer.finish_step(output)
+        output = producer.schedule()
+    else:
+        raise AssertionError("the prefill never finished")
+    _, block_ids = _block_ids(output, request.request_id, send=True)
+    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
+    for kv in producer.kv.values():
+        for block_id in block_ids:
+            kv[block_id] = torch.randint(
+                0, 256, kv[block_id].shape, generator=gen, dtype=torch.uint8
+            )
+    state_block = _state_block(producer, output, request.request_id, send=True)
+    split_state = None
+    if state_block is not None and producer.split_mamba:
+        conv = torch.randint(-(2**15), 2**15, (8, 8), generator=gen)
+        temporal = torch.randint(-(2**31), 2**31, (2, 8), generator=gen)
+        split_state = (
+            conv.to(torch.int16).view(torch.bfloat16),
+            temporal.to(torch.int32).view(torch.float32),
+        )
+        for rank, states in enumerate(producer.states):
+            shard = _split_shard(*split_state, producer.tp_size, rank)
+            states[state_block, : len(shard)] = shard
+    elif state_block is not None:
+        for states in producer.states:
+            states[state_block] = torch.randint(
+                0, 256, states[state_block].shape, generator=gen, dtype=torch.uint8
+            )
+    [engine_output] = producer.finish_step(output)[0].outputs
+    assert engine_output.finish_reason == FinishReason.LENGTH
+    # Connectors that send the checksums themselves get them in the next
+    # step's metadata.
+    meta = producer.schedule().kv_connector_metadata
+    if producer.connector == "MooncakeConnector":
+        # The router sends the request to both sides; the producer returns
+        # no kv_transfer_params.
+        assert engine_output.kv_transfer_params is None
+        params = {
+            "do_remote_decode": False,
+            "transfer_id": f"xfer-{request.request_id}",
+            "remote_engine_id": "producer",
+            "remote_bootstrap_addr": "http://producer:8998",
+        }
+        sent = meta.kv_checksums.get(request.request_id)
+    else:
+        params = engine_output.kv_transfer_params
+        assert params is not None
+        assert KV_TRANSFER_PARAMS_KEY in params
+        sent = getattr(meta, "push_finished_kv_checksums", {}).get(request.request_id)
+        assert (sent is not None) == (producer.connector == "NixlPushConnector")
+        if sent is not None:
+            # In push mode the proxy sends the consumer's request without the
+            # producer's response, so the checksums reach it with the KV.
+            params = {k: v for k, v in params.items() if k != KV_TRANSFER_PARAMS_KEY}
+    return _Transfer(params, sent, block_ids, state_block, split_state)
+

+def _copy_blocks(
+    producer: _Engine,
+    consumer: _Engine,
+    transfer: _Transfer,
+    start: int,
+    block_ids: list[int],
+    state_block: int | None = None,
+) -> None:
+    """The connector's transfer: the producer's tokens into the consumer's
+    blocks at the same token positions."""
+    p_size, c_size = producer.block_size, consumer.block_size
+    for layer, kv in consumer.kv.items():
+        for position, block_id in enumerate(block_ids, start):
+            for token in range(position * c_size, (position + 1) * c_size):
+                if token // p_size < len(transfer.block_ids):
+                    remote_block_id = transfer.block_ids[token // p_size]
+                    kv[block_id, :, token % c_size] = producer.kv[layer][
+                        remote_block_id, :, token % p_size
+                    ]
+    if state_block is not None and transfer.split_state is not None:
+        for rank, states in enumerate(consumer.states):
+            shard = _split_shard(*transfer.split_state, consumer.tp_size, rank)
+            states[state_block, : len(shard)] = shard
+    elif (
+        state_block is not None
+        and transfer.state_block is not None
+        and len(producer.states) == len(consumer.states)
+    ):
+        for p_states, c_states in zip(producer.states, consumer.states):
+            c_states[state_block] = p_states[transfer.state_block]
+

+def _load(
+    producer: _Engine,
+    consumer: _Engine,
+    request: Request,
+    transfer: _Transfer,
+    corrupt: str | None = None,
+    early: bool = False,
+):
+    """Start the load of ``request`` on the consumer, copy the producer's
+    blocks into the consumer's, and report the load finished with the
+    checksums the producer's connector sent, if any, or a step before it
+    finishes if ``early``."""
+    request.kv_transfer_params = {**transfer.params, "do_remote_prefill": True}
+    consumer.scheduler.add_request(request)
+    output = consumer.schedule()
+    assert request.status == RequestStatus.WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS
+    start, block_ids = _block_ids(output, request.request_id, send=False)
+    state_block = _state_block(consumer, output, request.request_id, send=False)
+    _copy_blocks(producer, consumer, transfer, start, block_ids, state_block)
+    if corrupt == "kv":
+        consumer.kv[LAYERS[1]][block_ids[-1], 0, 0, 0] ^= 1
+    elif corrupt == "state":
+        assert state_block is not None
+        consumer.states[0][state_block, MAMBA_STATE_BYTES - 1] ^= 1
+    elif corrupt == "last-replica":
+        # The last rank's copy of B, after its x rows of 16 bytes each.
+        assert state_block is not None
+        x_bytes = 4 // consumer.tp_size * 16
+        consumer.states[-1][state_block, x_bytes] ^= 1
+    received = {request.request_id: transfer.sent} if transfer.sent else None
+    if early:
+        consumer.finish_step(output, received=received)
+        output, received = consumer.schedule(), None
+    return consumer.finish_step(output, {request.request_id}, received)
+

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Connector-agnostic checksums of KV cache blocks.
+
+A checksum covers one block position of one KV cache group, over the
+unsharded model (all layers of the group, all KV heads):
+
+1. A slice is the KV of one layer and one KV head in the block: the K and V
+   of the block's tokens for that head. Laid out token by token and split
+   into little-endian 8-byte pieces, its checksum is::
+
+       s = sum_j x_j * (2 * j + 1)  mod 2**64
+
+   where piece ``x_j`` is piece ``p`` of the token at position ``t`` in the
+   request, ``j = t * P + p`` with ``P`` pieces per token.
+
+2. The block's checksum adds up the slices of every layer and head, each
+   times its own odd factor::
+
+       c = sum_{layer, head} m * s  mod 2**64,  m = 2 * (layer * H + head) + 1
+
+   where ``H = MAX_KV_HEADS_PER_LAYER``, a fixed bound on any layer's KV
+   heads, so that ``m`` does not depend on the model or how it is split.
+   Layers are numbered by the layer number in their names and heads
+   globally across TP; several caches of one layer (e.g. an attention's KV
+   and its indexer's) number their heads consecutively, in layer name order.
+
+Odd factors make any change to a single piece change ``c``, and distinct
+factors make misplaced data (swapped tokens, blocks, heads or layers) change
+it too. Numbering pieces from the request's start makes the checksums of
+consecutive blocks add up to that of the tokens they hold, so a producer and
+a consumer with different block sizes compare sums over the same tokens.
+
+A slice always lies whole on one TP rank, and each worker weighs its slices
+by their global layer and head, whatever its shard or memory layout. The
+parts from all TP ranks and PP stages therefore sum to ``c``, and a producer
+and a consumer can compare one value per (group, block position) regardless
+of their TP sizes, PP sizes or KV cache layouts.
+
+Replicated KV (MLA, or GQA with more TP ranks than KV heads) is tracked per
+replica: a partial checksum is keyed by ``(replicas, replica_index)`` of the
+layers it covers, so each consumer replica can be checked on its own.
+
+Mamba state is not per token: a group's block is the request's running
+state, at position 0. A layer whose TP split is known
+(``MambaSpec.state_splits``) has one slice per global row of its states,
+the TP-split dimension, whose pieces are its 2- or 4-byte elements read
+unsigned; other Mamba layers have one slice per TP shard, which only
+producers and consumers of equal TP sizes can compare.
+"""
+
+from collections.abc import Sequence
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+import numpy as np
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.triton_utils import HAS_TRITON
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+
+MAX_KV_HEADS_PER_LAYER = 1 << 16
+"""``H`` in the slice factor; groups with more KV heads per layer are not
+checksummed."""
+
+BLOCK_CHECKSUM_BYTES = 8
+"""Bytes per block of the ``KVChecksumWorker.init_block_checksums`` tensor:
+one int64."""
+
+ReplicaKey = tuple[int, int]
+"""``(replicas, replica_index)`` of the layers a partial checksum covers."""
+
+
+@dataclass
+class KVChecksumBlocks:
+    """The blocks of one request to checksum."""
+
+    # Tokens whose KV the blocks hold; slots of the last block at or past this
+    # count are not checksummed.
+    num_tokens: int
+    # Per KV cache group id, the position of the first block and the ids of the
+    # blocks at consecutive positions from there.
+    groups: dict[int, tuple[int, list[int]]]
+
+
+@dataclass
+class KVChecksumScheduled:
+    """The requests to checksum, by request id, set by the scheduler each step."""
+
+    # Scheduled to be checksummed after this step's forward, when their KV is final.
+    reqs_to_send: dict[str, KVChecksumBlocks] = field(default_factory=dict)
+    # Scheduled to be checksummed once the KV load started this step finishes.
+    reqs_to_recv: dict[str, KVChecksumBlocks] = field(default_factory=dict)
+    # Loads of offloaded KV started this step, checked once they finish against
+    # the checksums offloaded with the KV (``KVChecksumWorker.init_block_checksums``).
+    reqs_to_load: dict[str, KVChecksumBlocks] = field(default_factory=dict)
+
+
+@dataclass
+class KVChecksumGroup:
+    """One worker's partial checksums of one request's blocks in one group."""
+
+    # Position of the first row.
+    start: int
+    # The replica key of each column.
+    replica_keys: list[ReplicaKey]
+    # ``(num_positions, len(replica_keys))`` uint64 partial checksums.
+    values: np.ndarray
+    # For a load of offloaded KV, ``(num_positions,)`` uint64 checksums offloaded
+    # with the KV: each row's partial checksums, summed when the KV was offloaded.
+    stored: np.ndarray | None = None
+
+
+@dataclass
+class KVChecksumRecord:
+    """One worker's checksums for one step."""
+
+    pp_rank: int
+    tp_rank: int
+    # Partial checksums per request and group. Every request the worker
+    # processed this step has an entry, empty if none of its groups is here.
+    checksums: dict[str, dict[int, KVChecksumGroup]]
+    # Groups with layers on this worker that it cannot checksum.
+    skipped_groups: frozenset[int]
+    # Per transfer group, the sum of a hash (name, type, dtype) of each of this
+    # worker's layers in it. Summed over PP stages it identifies the group's layers.
+    fingerprints: dict[int, int]
+    # Producer checksums of loads received in connectors' own messages, per
+    # request; reported by the first worker only, as every worker receives them.
+    received: dict[str, bytes] = field(default_factory=dict)
+
+
+def num_valid_tokens(position: int, block_size: int, num_tokens: int) -> int:
+    """How many of the first ``num_tokens`` tokens block ``position`` holds."""
+    return min(block_size, max(0, num_tokens - position * block_size))
+
+
+def kv_checksum_platform_supported() -> bool:
+    """Whether this platform can run the KV checksum kernel."""
+    return HAS_TRITON and (
+        current_platform.is_cuda_alike() or current_platform.is_xpu()
+    )
+
+
+def kv_checksum_enabled(vllm_config: "VllmConfig") -> bool:
+    """Whether KV checksums are enabled; ``VllmConfig`` rejects setups that do
+    not support them."""
+    kv_transfer_config = vllm_config.kv_transfer_config
+    return kv_transfer_config is not None and kv_transfer_config.enable_kv_checksum
+
+
+def block_checksum_tags(block_hashes: Sequence[bytes], fingerprint: int) -> np.ndarray:
+    """The uint64 each block's offloaded checksum is XORed with, so that it
+    only matches the block it was stored for: its block hash and its group's
+    layers (``KVChecksumRecord.fingerprints``). Another TP or PP shard's KV
+    already checksums differently, as each worker weighs its own heads and
+    layers."""
+    tags = [int.from_bytes(h[:8], "little") for h in block_hashes]
+    return np.array(tags, dtype=np.uint64) ^ np.uint64(fingerprint)

+"""Triton kernel for the KV block checksums (see ``checksum.py``) of several
+layers of one layout, in one launch."""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+
+# Pieces one program sums.
+_CHUNK = 16 * 1024
+
+
+# One variant per layout; the output may have any number of columns.
+@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["out_stride"])
+def _layers_checksum_kernel(
+    pieces_ptr,  # int [num_blocks, kernel_blocks, heads, tokens, pieces]
+    stride_block,
+    stride_kernel_block,
+    stride_head,
+    stride_token,
+    stride_piece,
+    layers_ptr,  # int64 [num_layers, 3]: base address, first slice, column
+    block_ids_ptr,  # int64 [num_rows]
+    first_tokens_ptr,  # int64 [num_rows]
+    valid_tokens_ptr,  # int64 [num_rows]
+    out_ptr,  # int64 [num_rows, num_columns], accumulated into
+    out_stride,
+    kernel_blocks: tl.constexpr,
+    heads: tl.constexpr,
+    tokens: tl.constexpr,
+    num_pieces: tl.constexpr,
+    PIECE_BITS: tl.constexpr,
+    CHUNK: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+    SINGLE_LAYER: tl.constexpr,
+    ALIGNED: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    row = tl.program_id(0)
+    chunk = tl.program_id(1)
+    layer = tl.program_id(2)
+    if SINGLE_LAYER:
+        # The cache's own pointer, whose alignment Triton knows: up to a third
+        # faster than one loaded from the table.
+        layer_ptr = pieces_ptr
+    else:
+        layer_ptr = tl.load(layers_ptr + 3 * layer).to(
+            tl.pointer_type(pieces_ptr.dtype.element_ty)
+        )
+        if ALIGNED:
+            layer_ptr = tl.multiple_of(layer_ptr, 16)
+    first_slice = tl.load(layers_ptr + 3 * layer + 1).to(tl.uint64)
+    column = tl.load(layers_ptr + 3 * layer + 2)
+    block_id = tl.load(block_ids_ptr + row)
+    first_token = tl.load(first_tokens_ptr + row).to(tl.uint64)
+    valid_tokens = tl.load(valid_tokens_ptr + row)
+    block_ptr = layer_ptr + block_id * stride_block
+    slice_size = tokens * num_pieces
+    num_pieces_in_block = kernel_blocks * heads * slice_size
+    # uint64 arithmetic wraps around: mod 2**64.
+    acc = tl.zeros((BLOCK,), dtype=tl.uint64)
+    chunk_start = chunk * CHUNK
+    chunk_end = tl.minimum(chunk_start + CHUNK, num_pieces_in_block)
+    for start in range(chunk_start, chunk_end, BLOCK):
+        # One flat index over [kernel_block, head, token, piece].
+        offsets = start + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+        piece = offsets % num_pieces
+        token = offsets // num_pieces % tokens
+        head = offsets // slice_size % heads
+        kernel_block = offsets // (heads * slice_size)
+        token_index = kernel_block * tokens + token
+        mask = (offsets < chunk_end) & (token_index < valid_tokens)
+        x = tl.load(
+            block_ptr
+            + kernel_block.to(tl.int64) * stride_kernel_block
+            + head.to(tl.int64) * stride_head
+            + token.to(tl.int64) * stride_token
+            + piece.to(tl.int64) * stride_piece,
+            mask=mask,
+            other=0,
+        )
+        slice_weight = 2 * (first_slice + head.to(tl.uint64)) + 1
+        position = (first_token + token_index.to(tl.uint64)) * num_pieces + piece.to(
+            tl.uint64
+        )
+        # Pieces narrower than 64 bits count as unsigned.
+        x = x.to(tl.int64)
+        if PIECE_BITS < 64:
+            x = x & ((1 << PIECE_BITS) - 1)
+        x = x.to(tl.uint64, bitcast=True)
+        acc += x * (slice_weight * (2 * position + 1))
+    # Chunks and layers add up in any order: integer addition is exact.
+    tl.atomic_add(
+        out_ptr + row * out_stride + column, tl.sum(acc).to(tl.int64, bitcast=True)
+    )
+
+
+def layers_checksum(
+    pieces: torch.Tensor,
+    layers: torch.Tensor,
+    block_ids: torch.Tensor,
+    first_tokens: torch.Tensor,
+    valid_tokens: torch.Tensor,
+    out: torch.Tensor,
+    aligned: bool,
+) -> None:
+    """Add each layer's weighted piece sum of each block row into its column
+    of ``out``.
+
+    Args:
+        pieces: The first layer's cache as integer pieces
+            ``[num_blocks, kernel_blocks, heads, tokens, pieces]``, read as
+            unsigned. Every layer's cache has its shape, strides and dtype.
+        layers: ``[num_layers, 3]`` int64 on the device: each layer's cache
+            address, ``layer * H + head`` of its first head, and its column
+            of ``out``.
+        block_ids: ``[n]`` int64 logical block ids.
+        first_tokens: ``[n]`` int64 position in the request of each block's
+            first token.
+        valid_tokens: ``[n]`` int64 tokens to include from each block's start.
+        out: ``[n, num_columns]`` int64 accumulator with unit column stride.
+        aligned: Every address in ``layers`` is a multiple of 16 bytes.
+
+    """
+    _, kernel_blocks, heads, tokens, num_pieces = pieces.shape
+    num_pieces_in_block = kernel_blocks * heads * tokens * num_pieces
+    grid = (block_ids.shape[0], triton.cdiv(num_pieces_in_block, _CHUNK), len(layers))
+    _layers_checksum_kernel[grid](
+        pieces,
+        *pieces.stride(),
+        layers,
+        block_ids,
+        first_tokens,
+        valid_tokens,
+        out,
+        out.stride(0),
+        kernel_blocks,
+        heads,
+        tokens,
+        num_pieces,
+        PIECE_BITS=8 * pieces.element_size(),
+        CHUNK=_CHUNK,
+        BLOCK=min(triton.next_power_of_2(num_pieces_in_block), 1024),
+        SINGLE_LAYER=len(layers) == 1,
+        ALIGNED=aligned,
+    )

+producer request (``do_remote_decode``) when its prompt's KV is final, and a

+checked once it finishes against those checksums instead: each worker's
+checksums against the ones it offloaded (``KVChecksumWorker.init_block_checksums``).

+@dataclass
+class _LayerView:
+    """One layer's KV cache as integer pieces
+    ``[num_blocks, kernel_blocks, heads, tokens, pieces]``, read as unsigned.
+
+    A piece ``j`` of slice ``(layer, head)`` weighs ``m * (2 * j + 1)``, with
+    ``m = 2 * (layer * H + head) + 1`` for the global head (see
+    ``checksum.py``).
+    """
+
+    pieces: torch.Tensor
+    # ``layer * H + head`` of this rank's first head.
+    first_slice: int
+    # The replicas and replica index of this rank's heads.
+    replica_key: ReplicaKey

+class _FusedLayers:
+    """Layers of a group whose caches share one layout (shape, strides and
+    dtype), each adding into its column of the group's checksums in one
+    Triton launch."""
+
+    def __init__(self, views: list[_LayerView], columns: list[int]) -> None:
+        self.views = views
+        self.aligned = all(view.pieces.data_ptr() % 16 == 0 for view in views)
+        self.layers = torch.tensor(
+            [
+                [view.pieces.data_ptr(), view.first_slice, column]
+                for view, column in zip(views, columns)
+            ],
+            dtype=torch.int64,
+            device=views[0].pieces.device,
+        )
+
+    def accumulate(
+        self,
+        block_ids: torch.Tensor,
+        first_tokens: torch.Tensor,
+        valid_tokens: torch.Tensor,
+        out: torch.Tensor,
+    ) -> None:
+        """Add each layer's weighted sum of each block row into its column of``out``.
+
+        Args:
+            block_ids: ``[n]`` logical block ids on the device.
+            first_tokens: ``[n]`` position in the request of each block's first
+                token.
+            valid_tokens: ``[n]`` tokens to include from the start of each block.
+            out: ``[n, num_columns]`` int64 accumulator, wrapping around
+                (mod 2**64).
+
+        """
+        pieces = self.views[0].pieces
+        layers_checksum(
+            pieces,
+            self.layers,
+            block_ids,
+            first_tokens,
+            valid_tokens,
+            out,
+            self.aligned,
+        )
+
+    def warm_up(self, num_columns: int) -> None:
+        """Compile the Triton kernel now rather than in a serving step."""
+        device = self.views[0].pieces.device
+        zeros = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+        out = torch.zeros(1, num_columns, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+        self.accumulate(zeros, zeros, zeros, out)

+@dataclass
+class _GroupPlan:
+    """How a worker checksums a group's layers: one launch per cache layout,
+    adding into one column per replica key."""
+
+    replica_keys: list[ReplicaKey]
+    launches: list[_FusedLayers]
+
+    @classmethod
+    def create(cls, views: list[_LayerView]) -> "_GroupPlan | None":
+        if not views:
+            return None
+        replica_keys = list(dict.fromkeys(view.replica_key for view in views))
+        layouts: dict[tuple, list[_LayerView]] = defaultdict(list)
+        for view in views:
+            pieces = view.pieces
+            key = (pieces.dtype, pieces.device, pieces.shape, pieces.stride())
+            layouts[key].append(view)
+        launches = [
+            _FusedLayers(
+                same_layout,
+                [replica_keys.index(view.replica_key) for view in same_layout],
+            )
+            for same_layout in layouts.values()
+        ]
+        return cls(replica_keys, launches)

+    @property
+    def device(self) -> torch.device:
+        return self.launches[0].views[0].pieces.device

+def _layer_spec(group_spec: KVCacheSpec, layer_name: str) -> KVCacheSpec:

+def _group_fingerprint(group: KVCacheGroupSpec, tp_size: int) -> int:
+    """The sum of a hash of each of the group's layers on this worker."""
+    total = 0
+    for layer_name in group.layer_names:
+        spec = _layer_spec(group.kv_cache_spec, layer_name)
+        identity: tuple = (layer_name, type(spec).__name__)
+        if isinstance(spec, MambaSpec) and spec.state_splits is not None:
+            identity += (
+                _global_state_shapes(spec, tp_size),
+                [str(d) for d in spec.dtypes[: len(spec.state_splits)]],
+            )
+        elif isinstance(spec, MambaSpec):
+            states = _MAMBA_CHECKSUMMED_STATES
+            identity += (spec.shapes[:states], [str(d) for d in spec.dtypes[:states]])
+        else:
+            identity += (str(getattr(spec, "dtype", None)),)
+        digest = hashlib.sha256(repr(identity).encode()).digest()
+        total += int.from_bytes(digest[:8], "little")
+    return total % 2**64

+class _UnsupportedGroupError(Exception):
+    """A KV cache group whose layers cannot be checksummed."""

+def _tp_replicas(
+    spec: AttentionSpec, tp_size: int, uniform_kv_heads: int | None
+) -> int:
+    """Consecutive TP ranks holding the same KV heads of a layer.
+
+    Specs that declare ``max_tp_shards`` say how they shard, and MLA-type
+    caches that do not are held whole by every rank, as NIXL transfers them.
+    Other attention layers shard their KV heads across TP and, once TP exceeds them,
+    replicate one head on consecutive ranks. More than one head per rank thus
+    means no replicas, while one head per rank is ambiguous and is resolved
+    with the model's KV head count when every layer shares it.
+    """
+    if spec.max_tp_shards is not None:
+        return layer_tp_replicas(spec, tp_size, dcp_size=1)
+    if isinstance(spec, (MLAAttentionSpec, SlidingWindowMLASpec)):
+        return tp_size
+    if spec.num_kv_heads > 1 or tp_size == 1:
+        return 1
+    if uniform_kv_heads is None or tp_size % uniform_kv_heads:
+        raise _UnsupportedGroupError(
+            "its KV head replication across TP is unknown (one head per rank, "
+            "and the model's layers do not share one KV head count)"
+        )
+    return tp_size // uniform_kv_heads
+
+
+def _layer_module(layer_name: str) -> tuple[int, str]:
+    """The model-wide layer number in a layer name, the same on every rank,
+    and the name of its layer module (up to the number)."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.models.utils import extract_layer_index
+
+    try:
+        number = extract_layer_index(layer_name)
+    except AssertionError as e:
+        raise _UnsupportedGroupError(
+            f"layer {layer_name} has no single layer number"
+        ) from e
+    parts = layer_name.split(".")
+    end = next(i for i, part in enumerate(parts) if part.isdigit()) + 1
+    return number, ".".join(parts[:end])
+

+def _attention_pieces(
+    spec: KVCacheSpec,
+    cache: torch.Tensor,
+    num_blocks: int,
+    tp_size: int,
+    uniform_kv_heads: int | None,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, int, int]:
+    """An attention layer's 8-byte piece view, TP replicas and heads per rank."""
+    if not isinstance(spec, AttentionSpec) or not spec.has_layer_views:
+        raise _UnsupportedGroupError(
+            f"{type(spec).__name__} has no per-token KV blocks"
+        )
+    if spec.tokens_per_state != 1:
+        raise _UnsupportedGroupError(
+            f"{type(spec).__name__} stores {spec.tokens_per_state} tokens per state"
+        )
+    if spec.num_head_slots is not None:
+        raise _UnsupportedGroupError("its KV heads are packed into head slots")
+    pieces = _as_pieces(cache, num_blocks)
+    if pieces.shape[1] * pieces.shape[3] != spec.block_size:
+        raise _UnsupportedGroupError(
+            f"the kernel blocks of its cache of shape {tuple(cache.shape)} do not "
+            f"tile its {spec.block_size}-token blocks"
+        )
+    return pieces, _tp_replicas(spec, tp_size, uniform_kv_heads), spec.num_kv_heads

+def _mamba_pieces(
+    spec: MambaSpec, cache: torch.Tensor, num_blocks: int, tp_size: int
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, int, int]:
+    """Like ``_attention_pieces``, for a Mamba layer: each block's leading
+    ``_MAMBA_CHECKSUMMED_STATES`` states are one slice of one head and token.
+    """
+    covered = sum(
+        prod(shape) * get_dtype_size(dtype)
+        for shape, dtype in zip(
+            spec.shapes[:_MAMBA_CHECKSUMMED_STATES],
+            spec.dtypes[:_MAMBA_CHECKSUMMED_STATES],
+        )
+    )
+    if cache.dim() != 4 or cache.shape[0] != num_blocks or cache.shape[1:3] != (1, 1):
+        raise _UnsupportedGroupError(
+            f"its state cache of shape {tuple(cache.shape)} is not one page per block"
+        )
+    try:
+        pages = cache.view(torch.uint8)[:, 0, 0, :covered].view(torch.int64)
+    except RuntimeError as e:
+        raise _UnsupportedGroupError(
+            "its states or pages are not whole 8-byte pieces"
+        ) from e
+    replicas = tp_size if spec.tp_replicated else 1
+    return pages[:, None, None, None, :], replicas, 1
+
+
+def _global_state_shapes(spec: MambaSpec, tp_size: int) -> list[tuple]:
+    """Per split state: its global segment sizes and its other dimensions."""
+    assert spec.state_splits is not None
+    shapes = []
+    for shape, split in zip(spec.shapes, spec.state_splits):
+        segments = tuple(size * tp_size // r for size, r in split.segments)
+        others = shape[: split.axis] + shape[split.axis + 1 :]
+        shapes.append((segments, others))
+    return shapes
+
+
+def _mamba_rows(
+    spec: MambaSpec, cache: torch.Tensor, num_blocks: int, number: int, tp_size: int
+) -> list["_LayerCache"]:
+    """A Mamba layer's TP-split states, each global row (the TP-split
+    dimension, see ``MambaStateSplit``) one slice of its elements, read as
+    unsigned 2- or 4-byte pieces. Slices are numbered across the layer's
+    states in their global order, so a rank holds those of its shard of each
+    segment whatever the TP size.
+    """
+    assert spec.state_splits is not None
+    if cache.dim() != 4 or cache.shape[0] != num_blocks or cache.shape[1:3] != (1, 1):
+        raise _UnsupportedGroupError(
+            f"its state cache of shape {tuple(cache.shape)} is not one page per block"
+        )
+    pages = cache.view(torch.uint8)[:, 0, 0]
+    caches: list[_LayerCache] = []
+    offset = global_rows = 0
+    for shape, dtype, split in zip(spec.shapes, spec.dtypes, spec.state_splits):
+        size = get_dtype_size(dtype)
+        if size not in (2, 4):
+            raise _UnsupportedGroupError(f"its {dtype} states are not 2 or 4 bytes")
+        nbytes = prod(shape) * size
+        if offset + nbytes > pages.shape[1]:
+            raise _UnsupportedGroupError("its state cache is smaller than its states")
+        state = pages[:, offset : offset + nbytes]
+        offset += nbytes
+        try:
+            # [blocks, rows, pieces]: the TP-split dimension, then the rest.
+            elements = state.view(torch.int16 if size == 2 else torch.int32)
+            rows = elements.unflatten(1, shape).movedim(split.axis + 1, 1)
+            if rows.dim() > 3:
+                rows = rows.view(num_blocks, rows.shape[1], -1)
+        except RuntimeError as e:
+            raise _UnsupportedGroupError("its states cannot be viewed by rows") from e
+        if sum(local for local, _ in split.segments) != rows.shape[1]:
+            raise _UnsupportedGroupError("its state splits do not match its states")
+        local_rows = 0
+        for local, replicas in split.segments:
+            caches.append(
+                _LayerCache(
+                    number,
+                    rows[:, None, local_rows : local_rows + local, None],
+                    replicas,
+                    heads=local,
+                    first_head=global_rows,
+                )
+            )
+            local_rows += local
+            global_rows += local * tp_size // replicas
+    return caches
+
+
+def _as_pieces(cache: torch.Tensor, num_blocks: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """A ``[blocks, kernel_blocks, heads, tokens, pieces]`` 8-byte piece view."""
+    if cache.dim() != 4 or cache.shape[0] % num_blocks:
+        raise _UnsupportedGroupError(
+            f"its cache of shape {tuple(cache.shape)} does not hold {num_blocks} blocks"
+        )
+    try:
+        pieces = cache.view(torch.uint8).view(torch.int64)
+    except RuntimeError as e:
+        raise _UnsupportedGroupError(
+            "its KV cells or strides are not whole 8-byte pieces"
+        ) from e
+    # Kernel blocks subdivide manager blocks contiguously (group_kernel_blocks).
+    return pieces.unflatten(0, (num_blocks, -1))

+@dataclass
+class _LayerCache:
+    """One distinct KV cache of a group, or segment of a Mamba state, under the
+    lowest layer number using it. Rank ``r`` holds shard ``r // replicas``:
+    the ``heads`` slices from ``first_head + shard * heads`` in the layer.
+    """
+
+    number: int
+    pieces: torch.Tensor
+    replicas: int
+    heads: int
+    first_head: int = 0
+
+
+def _build_layer_views(
+    group: KVCacheGroupSpec,
+    kv_caches: dict[str, torch.Tensor],
+    num_blocks: int,
+    tp_rank: int,
+    tp_size: int,
+    uniform_kv_heads: int | None,
+) -> list[_LayerView]:
+    """The views of a group's layers, each KV cache counted once.
+
+    Raises:
+        _UnsupportedGroupError: If the group cannot be checksummed.
+
+    """
+    if group.host_resident:
+        raise _UnsupportedGroupError("its KV is host-resident")
+    # KV-sharing layers alias their target's cache: count each cache once,
+    # under the lowest (layer number, name) that uses it.
+    owners: dict[tuple[int, tuple[int, ...]], tuple[int, str]] = {}
+    entries: dict[tuple[int, tuple[int, ...]], list[_LayerCache]] = {}
+    for layer_name in group.layer_names:
+        spec = _layer_spec(group.kv_cache_spec, layer_name)
+        cache = kv_caches.get(layer_name)
+        if cache is None:
+            raise _UnsupportedGroupError(f"layer {layer_name} has no KV cache")
+        if isinstance(spec, MambaSpec) and isinstance(
+            group.kv_cache_spec, UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs
+        ):
+            # The scheduler picks a Mamba group's state block by its group spec.
+            raise _UnsupportedGroupError("its Mamba layers have different specs")
+        number, _ = _layer_module(layer_name)
+        identity = (cache.data_ptr(), cache.stride())
+        if identity in owners:
+            owners[identity] = min(owners[identity], (number, layer_name))
+            continue
+        owners[identity] = (number, layer_name)
+        if isinstance(spec, MambaSpec) and spec.state_splits is not None:
+            entries[identity] = _mamba_rows(spec, cache, num_blocks, number, tp_size)
+        elif isinstance(spec, MambaSpec):
+            pieces, replicas, heads = _mamba_pieces(spec, cache, num_blocks, tp_size)
+            entries[identity] = [_LayerCache(number, pieces, replicas, heads)]
+        else:
+            pieces, replicas, heads = _attention_pieces(
+                spec, cache, num_blocks, tp_size, uniform_kv_heads
+            )
+            entries[identity] = [_LayerCache(number, pieces, replicas, heads)]
+
+    # The caches of one layer module (e.g. an attention's KV and its indexer's,
+    # always on one PP stage) take consecutive slices, in layer name order.
+    layers: list[_LayerCache] = []
+    modules: dict[int, str] = {}
+    next_head: dict[int, int] = defaultdict(int)
+    for identity, (number, name) in sorted(owners.items(), key=lambda item: item[1]):
+        module = _layer_module(name)[1]
+        if modules.setdefault(number, module) != module:
+            raise _UnsupportedGroupError(
+                f"layers {modules[number]} and {module} share a layer number"
+            )
+        for layer in entries[identity]:
+            layer.number = number
+            layer.first_head += next_head[number]
+        next_head[number] = max(
+            layer.first_head + layer.heads * (tp_size // layer.replicas)
+            for layer in entries[identity]
+        )
+        layers.extend(entries[identity])
+    if any(heads > MAX_KV_HEADS_PER_LAYER for heads in next_head.values()):
+        raise _UnsupportedGroupError(
+            f"a layer has more than {MAX_KV_HEADS_PER_LAYER} KV heads"
+        )
+    views = []
+    for layer in layers:
+        shard, replica = divmod(tp_rank, layer.replicas)
+        views.append(
+            _LayerView(
+                layer.pieces,
+                first_slice=layer.number * MAX_KV_HEADS_PER_LAYER
+                + layer.first_head
+                + shard * layer.heads,
+                replica_key=(layer.replicas, replica),
+            )
+        )
+    return views
+

+@dataclass
+class _GroupBatch:
+    """The rows of one KV cache group to checksum in one pass."""
+
+    # ``(req_id, start_position, num_rows)`` per request, in row order.
+    segments: list[tuple[str, int, int]] = field(default_factory=list)
+    block_ids: list[int] = field(default_factory=list)
+    # The request's number of tokens, per segment.
+    num_tokens: list[int] = field(default_factory=list)
+
+    def rows(self, block_size: int) -> np.ndarray:
+        """The ``[block_ids, first_tokens, valid_tokens]`` of the rows."""
+        starts = np.array([start for _, start, _ in self.segments], dtype=np.int64)
+        lengths = np.array([n for _, _, n in self.segments], dtype=np.int64)
+        first_rows = np.cumsum(lengths) - lengths
+        positions = np.arange(len(self.block_ids), dtype=np.int64)
+        positions += np.repeat(starts - first_rows, lengths)
+        first_tokens = positions * block_size
+        num_tokens = np.repeat(np.array(self.num_tokens, dtype=np.int64), lengths)
+        valid_tokens = np.clip(num_tokens - first_tokens, 0, block_size)
+        block_ids = np.array(self.block_ids, dtype=np.int64)
+        return np.stack([block_ids, first_tokens, valid_tokens])
+

+class PendingKVChecksums:
+    """A worker's KV checksums of one step, until they reach host memory.
+
+    ``post_forward`` queues the checksum kernels on the main stream. The model
+    runner then calls ``enqueue_async_cpu_copy`` on its output copy stream, ordered
+    after them, and reads the record it returns once that copy is done.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        pp_rank: int,
+        tp_rank: int,
+        skipped_groups: frozenset[int],
+        fingerprints: dict[int, int],
+        received: dict[str, bytes],
+    ):
+        self._rank = (pp_rank, tp_rank)
+        self._skipped_groups = skipped_groups
+        self._fingerprints = fingerprints
+        self._received = received
+        self._req_ids: list[str] = []
+        # (group id, segments, replica keys, [rows, len(replica keys)] int64
+        # values, [rows] int64 offloaded checksums or None) per checksum pass
+        # of a group: the loads and the sends of one step are separate passes
+        # over the same groups.
+        self._groups: list[
+            tuple[
+                int,
+                list[tuple[str, int, int]],
+                list[ReplicaKey],
+                torch.Tensor,
+                torch.Tensor | None,
+            ]
+        ] = []
+
+    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
+        return bool(self._req_ids or self._received)
+
+    def add_requests(self, req_ids: Iterable[str]) -> None:
+        self._req_ids.extend(req_ids)
+
+    def add_group(
+        self,
+        group_id: int,
+        segments: list[tuple[str, int, int]],
+        replica_keys: list[ReplicaKey],
+        values: torch.Tensor,
+        stored: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        self._groups.append((group_id, segments, replica_keys, values, stored))
+
+    def enqueue_async_cpu_copy(self) -> KVChecksumRecord:
+        """Enqueue the asynchronous D2H copy; call on the output copy stream,
+        after it waits for the main stream."""
+        checksums: dict[str, dict[int, KVChecksumGroup]] = {
+            req_id: {} for req_id in self._req_ids
+        }
+        for (
+            group_id,
+            segments,
+            replica_keys,
+            device_values,
+            device_stored,
+        ) in self._groups:
+            values = device_values.to("cpu", non_blocking=True).numpy()
+            values = values.view(np.uint64)
+            stored = None
+            if device_stored is not None:
+                stored = device_stored.to("cpu", non_blocking=True).numpy()
+                stored = stored.view(np.uint64)
+            row = 0
+            for req_id, start, num_rows in segments:
+                checksums[req_id][group_id] = KVChecksumGroup(
+                    start,
+                    replica_keys,
+                    values[row : row + num_rows],
+                    None if stored is None else stored[row : row + num_rows],
+                )
+                row += num_rows
+        return KVChecksumRecord(
+            *self._rank,
+            checksums,
+            self._skipped_groups,
+            self._fingerprints,
+            self._received,
+        )
+

+class KVChecksumWorker:
+    """Computes the KV checksums the scheduler asks a worker for.
+
+    Requests to send are checksummed in the step that finishes their KV.
+    Requests to receive are checksummed in the step whose transfer results
+    report their load finished, before any later step can write their blocks.
+    A connector that offloads KV and loads it back can offload checksums with
+    it (``init_block_checksums``), which the loads are checked against.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        kv_cache_config: KVCacheConfig,
+        kv_caches: dict[str, torch.Tensor],
+        tp_rank: int,
+        tp_size: int,
+        pp_rank: int,
+        uniform_kv_heads: int | None,
+        draft_layer_names: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
+    ):
+        self.tp_rank = tp_rank
+        self.pp_rank = pp_rank
+        # Per group: loads check every replica of this worker's layers, while
+        # a producer only needs the first replica of each layer, as any replica
+        # describes the same KV and consumers check each of theirs against it.
+        self._recv_plans: dict[int, _GroupPlan] = {}
+        self._send_plans: dict[int, _GroupPlan] = {}
+        self._block_sizes: dict[int, int] = {}
+        skipped_groups = set()

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

Thanks for the checksum+tag design. It is a nice way to catch misplacement after the fact, and I appreciate the explicit limitation note.

One scenario from Mooncake Issue(https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/issues/4491), I'm unsure this can catch: a batch_get times out, stored_requests[req_id] hits zero, and vLLM releases the KV block—but the underlying RDMA writes may still be in flight. If Request B then reuses that block, we have two concurrent writers to the same memory. Since the checksum is a post-hoc snapshot (computed after the producer considers the write "done"), it seems like a late-arriving write after that snapshot—or a checksum computed during the race—wouldn't be detected at the moment of concurrent write, only (maybe) by a future consumer.

So does this PR actually defend against this concurrent-write-to-the-same-block case, or is that outside what a post-hoc checksum can detect? If the latter, are there other mitigations (e.g., waiting for Mooncake's physical DRAINED state, or a write barrier like #62282 does for P2P), or is the real fix only on the Mooncake side as the limitations note suggests?
